chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the finger, its wergild is one-tenth of the full blood money if it is cut off from its root or becomes paralyzed.
He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the fingers, are they equal in wergild?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about the teeth, so he said: Their wergild is the same'.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for cutting off a finger or tooth in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the proportional valuation of bodily injuries, establishing that a severed or paralyzed finger incurs one-tenth of the full *diyah*, while affirming the uniformity in compensation for all fingers and teeth. This ruling reflects the systematic application of *qisas* and *diyah* principles in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring equitable restitution for physical harm. The hadith underscores the precision required in calculating blood money, a key component of Islamic penal law derived from the Prophet’s tradition.
